newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures called to open flat to up 0.10.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures called to open flat to up 0.10.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent firmer based on market orders at 1019 EDT, floor sources said.

They expect trade to remain rangebound and thin ahead of Tuesday's supply and demand estimates. Industry sources estimated this year's harvest between 17.47 million and 18.15 million 480-lb bales, with most estimates clustered near the high side of the range.
On July 11, USDA put this year's crop at 18.00 million bales, down from 18.94 million bales produced in 1996/97 (Aug/July).
Growing conditions, meantime, remain mostly favorable for cotton in Texas. Recent rains helped the developing crop in the Delta, but more rain is needed, Weather Services Corp, said.
Friday, most-active December cotton closed down 0.09 cent at 74.31 cents a lb, with the rest 0.07 firmer to 0.27 lower.
An estimated 16,000 lots changed hands Friday.
Resistance was pegged at 75.00 to 75.20 cents for December delivery, with support at 74.00 to 73.80 cents.
